name: How do I choose between plaster, pebble, and quartz for pool renovation?

mainEntity.name: Which interior finish is best for a renovated pool: plaster, pebble, or quartz?
mainEntity.text: Which interior finish is best for a renovated pool: plaster, pebble, or quartz?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each interior finish has tradeoffs. Standard plaster is usually the least expensive and gives a classic smooth look, but it tends to wear faster than premium finishes. Pebble finishes generally last longer and handle heavy use well, though they have more texture underfoot. Quartz finishes sit between the two, offering improved durability and color options while keeping a smoother feel than pebble. In warm climates like Los Angeles, many homeowners choose quartz or pebble because they better support a luxury look over time. The best choice depends on how often the pool is used, whether you want a softer feel or maximum longevity, and how much maintenance you are willing to accept. Ask contractors for samples, maintenance expectations, and typical lifespan so you can compare beyond just the upfront price. The right finish is the one that fits both lifestyle and design goals.
acceptedAnswer.description: Plaster is the most affordable interior finish, pebble is the most durable and textured, and quartz sits in the middle with a smoother feel and better longevity than basic plaster. The best choice depends on budget, comfort, maintenance preferences, and desired look.
